title: 2011 AMC 10B Problem 23
statement: What is the hundreds digit of \(2011^{2011}?\)

solutions.text:
Because \(2011\equiv11\pmod{1000}\), it is enough to find \(11^{2011}=(10+1)^{2011}\) modulo \(1000\).

All terms with \(10^3\) or higher are divisible by \(1000\), so only the first three terms matter: \[1+2011\cdot10+\binom{2011}{2}10^2.\]

Modulo \(1000\), this is \[ \begin{aligned} &1+11\cdot10+\dfrac{2011\cdot2010}{2}\cdot100 \\ &\quad \equiv1+110+500=611 \end{aligned} \].

The hundreds digit is therefore \(6\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: In \((10+1)^{2011}\), terms with \(10^3\) or higher do not affect the last three digits
